Balancing a real polling lead for the Democrat against historical GOP overperformance and TX's red lean, this looks close to a coin flip with a modest tilt toward Republicans still winning.

results.reasoning: Multiple forecast sources (AccuWeather, NWS point forecasts) for Oct 20, 2026 in Miami show scattered showers/thunderstorms with precipitation chances ranging roughly 20-60%, and an active Rip Current Statement spanning Oct 18-22 indicates an unsettled weather pattern (onshore flow/front) affecting South Florida during this window. October is Miami's wet season with climatological rain on ~25-40% of days, but the specific forecast guidance for this date (e.g., AccuWeather's 'morning thunderstorm' call, NWS 30-60% PoP) pushes the probability of measurable (≥0.01in) precipitation at KMIA notably above the seasonal base rate.
results.key_findings: ["AccuWeather 10-day forecast for Miami/Miami Intl Airport explicitly lists 'A morning thunderstorm' / 'Humid; an afternoon t-storm' for Oct 20, 2026","NWS point forecasts for Miami Dade coastal zone show chance of precipitation around 30-60% for the Oct 19-21 period","A Rip Current Statement was in effect Oct 18 02:00 AM EDT through Oct 22 08:00 PM EDT, consistent with an active onshore/frontal weather pattern bringing shower activity","Miami's October climatology shows roughly 7-12 rainy days per month (~25-40% of days), establishing a meaningful baseline even without an active system"]

Unfilled makers are missed trades, not losses.

xvenue.read: polyMoves = minutes where Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c; staleKalshi = of those, Kalshi's same-minute quote was still crossable after its 7.000000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (avgStaleEdgeC = cents of edge per share); kalshiSameMin/NextMin = Kalshi moved the same way that minute / the next; kalshiLeads = Kalshi moved first and Polymarket followed. A Kalshi lane is worth building only if staleRate x avgStaleEdgeC is meaningfully positive over many games. us* = the same for Polymarket US (taker 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p)); kUsCross = minutes where buying on one US-legal venue and selling on the other cleared both taker fees (the only fully legal arbitrage pair for a US operator).

usLane.read: Paper only: each event is a hypothetical taker fill on Polymarket US at the sampled quote (px, qty = shares shown at that price; one event per game minute, on the leg the US instrument quotes). tradable = the subset with at least 50 shares shown (usd = dollars on the shown size, capped at 1000 shares) in a minute where global Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c and the US quote was still crossable after the 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (edgeC = cents of edge at entry). marks.* = cents per share after the entry fee, marked at global Polymarket's mid 1/5/15/60 minutes later and at the end of the game (final), and at settlement (0/1); exit fees and the US spread are not charged on those. marks.x5 / marks.x15 are the round trip: closed on the Polymarket US book 5 / 15 minutes later (the bid for a buy, the ask for a sell, so the spread is paid) with the exit taker fee charged too - what a scalping lane would actually have booked. roiPct = avg mark pnl / avg entry price. noData = horizon passed with no sample. Decision rule (docs/PROFIT-AVENUES.md Part 2): after ~200 events, a Polymarket US lane is worth building only if the round trip (x5 or x15) is positive on the tradable subset with a hit rate above 50%, or settle is; the real-money flip stays the operator's call.

cryptoFv.read: model = driftless lognormal at the asset's 30-day realized vol (sigma); gap = model - market for the YES side. Far-dated dip/reach tails trade above the model by design (fat tails): treat a big tail gap as a model warning, not an edge.
